business_problem: Microsoft wanted to modernize corporate spend-risk monitoring because existing compliance testing was siloed across organizations, relied on random sampling and periodic reviews, and made it hard to spot anomalies quickly or manage policies consistently across its global footprint.
solution_summary: Microsoft expanded its longstanding relationship with EY to build the Spend Risk Monitoring Modernization program around EY Virtual, a microservices-based continuous monitoring platform on Microsoft Azure Data Factory. EY configured the Spend Analytics application to ingest Microsoft's global spending transactions, test them against risk triggers and signals, and use advanced analytics, AI and machine learning to identify anomalous activity. High-risk items flow into EY Controls, which runs on Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Power Automate so review teams can investigate and report findings without manual handoffs. Power BI provides reporting back to Microsoft, while feedback loops from completed reviews are fed back into EY Virtual to improve future screening. The result is an end-to-end, automated compliance workflow that replaces fragmented sampling with real-time risk-based monitoring across territories, business units and controls.

data_flow: Transaction data from Microsoft business units is ingested through Azure Data Factory into EY Virtual, where Spend Analytics tests each record against risk triggers and machine learning signals. High-risk anomalies move into EY Controls on Dynamics 365 and Power Automate for human review, Power BI reports the results, and the completed outcomes feed back into EY Virtual to refine future screening.
business_outcome: Microsoft replaced fragmented random sampling with a scalable risk-based monitoring program that reviews global spend in real time, focuses reviewers on the riskiest transactions, consolidates siloed compliance programs, and removes substantial manual effort while improving coverage and consistency.
